title: Default to no animation
principle: The best animation is often no animation. Emil Kowalski’s You Don’t Need Animations: when users open a tool with a clear goal hundreds of times a day, delight becomes friction. Frequency of use is the deciding variable—hover flair, list selection, and keyboard navigation usually lose to instant response. Ship restraint on purpose.
procedure: List surfaces by daily frequency (power tools, lists, shortcuts vs rare feedback, onboarding, marketing).
Delete motion on high-frequency and keyboard-driven paths by default.
Keep motion only where purpose is clear and frequency is low enough that delight won’t sour.
If unsure, A/B with yourself: toggle J/K style open with and without motion—pick the one that still feels good after twenty reps.
Document the ‘no motion’ decisions so the next agent doesn’t ‘polish’ them back in.
examplePrompts:
Apply animation restraint (Emil Kowalski — You Don’t Need Animations):
1) Rank every animated element by how often a power user will see it per day.
2) Remove animations from anything likely >20×/day and from all keyboard-initiated actions.
3) Keep at most 1–2 low-frequency delight motions if they have a purpose.
4) Do not replace deleted motion with slower ‘elegant’ fades.
Return a before/after inventory.
This command palette animates on open and on highlight move. Strip both. Make highlight follow keys instantly. Justify any remaining motion in one sentence or delete it.
promptWhy: Frequency ranking makes delete decisions mechanical instead of taste-argumentative.
Palette example targets the classic AI failure: decorative motion on a workhorse control.
tips: Raycast opens with no animation—and that is the optimal daily experience.
Rare morphing feedback widgets can delight; the same morph every hour becomes annoyance.
Restraint pairs with remove-ai-tells: motion-as-chrome is an AI tell.

workedExamples.title: Command palette vs marketing hero
workedExamples.after: Palette: instant. Hero explain-motion: kept with a purpose sentence.
workedExamples.body: Emil contrasts daily tools (no animation) with purposeful marketing motion. Frequency splits the decision. Cite: emilkowal.ski/ui/you-dont-need-animations.

workedExamples.title: List highlight lag
workedExamples.body: Arrow-key list selection with animated highlight feels delayed and disconnected. Instant highlight wins for high-frequency navigation—demoed in the public essay.

workedExamples.title: Quiet Folio desk
workedExamples.body: This catalog’s motion lab uses short, reduced-motion-aware recipes. Most chrome stays still; restraint is part of the letterpress aesthetic.

antiPatterns: Adding enter animations to every panel ‘for consistency’.
Animating keyboard highlight or focus rings with duration.
Reintroducing deleted motion in a later ‘make it alive’ pass without re-checking frequency.
checklist: Frequency inventory exists for animated surfaces.
High-frequency UI has no decorative motion.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: Which change would be harder to understand without movement?
avoidWhen: Do not stack stagger, tilt, blur and entrance effects on the same element.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Default to no animation” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
acceptance: Toggle twice before a transition ends: the latest state wins. With reduced motion, all information and controls remain available immediately.
Frequency inventory exists for animated surfaces.
High-frequency UI has no decorative motion.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Only state or spatial continuity needs motion; repeated actions stay immediate.

comparison.bad: Every result animates in after each keystroke, delaying comparison.
comparison.good: Results update immediately; a brief emphasis on selection confirms only the changed state.
comparison.impact: Only state or spatial continuity needs motion; repeated actions stay immediate.
